statusDetail: Coverage-complete model-led audit across representative home, section, article, breaking-news, account-entry and error templates.

page.framework: Mixed legacy/server templates with client-rendered widgets and advertising integrations
page.notes: Public Hebrew news publisher. Core raw HTML includes metadata but article/listing content has very low no-JS overlap.

checkOutcomes.method: Paired screenshots under light and dark preference
checkOutcomes.evidence: Light/dark captures are visually identical.
Ten animations remained active, including infinite animations.
Preference matched but no contrast/forced-colors adaptation was present.
No view-transition use was found for MPA navigation.
No intentional parallax, scrollytelling, or scroll-linked reveal requiring a scroll timeline was identified on sampled templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: No intentional parallax, scrollytelling, or scroll-linked reveal requiring a scroll timeline was identified on sampled templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No primary pull, swipe-to-remove, or other gesture-driven task was present in the sampled editorial and login journeys.
checkOutcomes.reason: No primary pull, swipe-to-remove, or other gesture-driven task was present in the sampled editorial and login journeys.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Long pages lacked scroll-state query or progress signaling.
No tooltip or viewport-edge anchored menu was required by the sampled primary journeys; the blocking consent modal is not an anchored overlay.
checkOutcomes.reason: No tooltip or viewport-edge anchored menu was required by the sampled primary journeys; the blocking consent modal is not an anchored overlay.

checkOutcomes.method: Visual hierarchy, link and recovery-path inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Persistent labelled navigation, section headings, real internal hrefs, and a clear 404 home action orient users despite density.
Full-page consent interstitial obscures content.
Blocking modal uses generic divs; no dialog/popover exists.
Homepage contains 1,427 links/438 images plus blocking and promotional chrome.
Viewport is fixed at 1240 and scaled to 0.29 on mobile.
No container-query signal across five templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Hundreds of sub-24px targets and invisible sampled focus states.
Brand, news headlines, section labels and article titles make the editorial purpose and next reading actions clear.
Consent modal blocks the representative read-an-article flow.
Unknown URL shows a specific error heading and a home-page recovery link.
Article CLS 0.466; 23/23 sampled article images lacked dimensions.
23 long tasks and severe TBT.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR summary confirmed against image DOM
checkOutcomes.evidence: 607 requests/16.98MB and extensive unoptimized image delivery.
2.8–2.9MiB unused JavaScript and 500–568KiB unused CSS estimated.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility and image DOM audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: Unnamed links/buttons and missing image alternatives were found.
Five home and two article contrast failures.

checkOutcomes.method: Keyboard focus probe and heading inventory
checkOutcomes.evidence: First 25 sampled controls showed no visible focus; consent adds multiple H1s to document structure.
Fixed 1240px canvas shrinks Hebrew text to an illegible scale on mobile.
Shrink-to-fit viewport, hundreds of tiny targets, and captionless article video.
16 home and 7 article console errors.
Doctype/charset pass, but nearly all homepage images lack intrinsic dimensions and many are oversized.
Inspector issues and broken source-map mappings were reported.
Login template has no meta description.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse SEO, viewport and raw HTML comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: Non-crawlable links, fixed-width viewport and only 4–10% raw content coverage.
Pages have canonicals and robots is reachable, but /sitemap.xml is a 404 and no sitemap is advertised.
Editorial templates expose 2–3 JSON-LD blocks and 6–7 Open Graph fields matching visible titles.
Missing HSTS/nosniff/referrer/permissions headers and insecure cookie attributes.

checkOutcomes.method: Tracker and HAR primitives plus consent flow
checkOutcomes.evidence: 71 third-party origins and 27 known trackers with asymmetric consent choices.
No on-load permission request was detected, but relevant auth flow lacks passkeys.
Frame protection exists, but HSTS, robust CSP directives, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent.

checkOutcomes.method: Raw HTML/rendered DOM comparison with crawler screenshots
checkOutcomes.evidence: Article/news are classified as JS shells with 4–5% content overlap and blank crawler views.
Across five templates, content rendered, consent could be managed, and the explicit invalid route reached a stable recovery page.
This public news MPA is not presented as an installable app; no offline app intent is declared, so PWA installability is not required for this check.
checkOutcomes.reason: This public news MPA is not presented as an installable app; no offline app intent is declared, so PWA installability is not required for this check.

checkOutcomes.evidence: A missing URL produces a specific “page does not exist” state and a link back home rather than a blank shell.

checkOutcomes.method: Root attributes, computed direction and CSS signal probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: lang=he but computed direction is ltr; physical CSS overwhelmingly dominates.

checkOutcomes.method: Rendered locale/content inspection across home, breaking news and weather links
checkOutcomes.evidence: Dates, temperatures, breaking-news times and surrounding labels are rendered in Hebrew conventions consistently on sampled pages.
No user-created event, cross-time-zone schedule, recurring interval, or editable time data was present in the sampled editorial/login journeys.
checkOutcomes.reason: No user-created event, cross-time-zone schedule, recurring interval, or editable time data was present in the sampled editorial/login journeys.

checkOutcomes.method: Garbage-collected baseline/post heap plus in-session metrics after 10 scroll cycles
checkOutcomes.evidence: Heap/DOM grew materially after repeated traversal; confidence is medium because dynamic feed loading may explain part of growth.

checkOutcomes.method: Heap summary and live DOM sample
checkOutcomes.evidence: Baseline is 147.4MB/2.05M heap nodes and 13,735 live DOM elements.
No Detached* constructor appeared among the largest retained constructor populations; listener accumulation was not directly exposed, so confidence is medium.

principleOutcomes.reason: No agent-facing capability or declared agent integration intent was present; for this emerging contextual principle, absence is an opportunity rather than a failure. No product task requiring on-device inference was exposed in the sampled editorial/login journeys, and no agent-facing intent is declared.

paths.description: Homepage: primary news discovery, navigation, consent, responsive, performance and network template.
News section listing: representative section/index template and no-JS discoverability.
News article: representative content/detail template, media, stability, accessibility and no-JS rendering.
Breaking-news listing: dense frequently updated list and target-size/navigation behavior.
Account entry: representative form/auth journey, autocomplete, invalid input and modern authentication.

findings.summary: The interface does not meaningfully adapt to dark, reduced-motion, or increased-contrast preferences.
findings.evidence: Light and dark mobile screenshots are visually identical; under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, ten animations remain running (including four 6–17.2s animations and six infinite animations); the contrast probe found no prefers-contrast/forced-colors CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Define semantic light/dark color tokens with color-scheme and prefers-color-scheme, stop non-essential motion under prefers-reduced-motion, and add forced-colors/prefers-contrast adaptations.

findings.summary: Navigation changes are abrupt and do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS/DOM probes on five templates found no view-transition signal; the site is an MPA with many cross-document navigation links.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } for same-origin pages, with reduced-motion handling and stable view-transition-name assignments for shared elements.

findings.summary: Long pages do not expose modern scroll-state-aware navigation chrome.
findings.evidence: The 15,291px homepage and 7,467px article probes found no scroll-state/container-query or scroll-progress implementation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a sticky header with scroll-state container queries or a lightweight scroll progress indicator, while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial blocks the full page on every fresh visit.
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, article, and crawler-rendered screenshots show an opaque modal and dimmed page before any interaction; initial actions are only “Consent” and “Manage options”.
findings.suggestedFix: Present a compact, non-obscuring consent notice where lawful, include equally prominent accept/reject controls, and preserve access to core editorial content.

findings.summary: The blocking consent UI is built from generic divs rather than a dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: DOM probes found zero <dialog> or popover elements while a fixed .fc-consent-root/.fc-dialog-overlay covered most of the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement modal behavior with <dialog>, labelled by visible headings, with correct focus containment, escape/cancel behavior, and a non-modal fallback.

findings.summary: The homepage is extremely dense with repeated navigation, cards, ads, and recommendation chrome.
findings.evidence: The first mobile capture is a scaled 15,291px page with a blocking modal; the DOM includes 1,427 links and 438 images.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce duplicate navigation and recommendation modules, prioritize editorial hierarchy, and defer secondary/ad content below the initial reading task.

findings.summary: The site forces a 1,240px desktop layout on a 360px mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: meta viewport is width=1240 on all five templates; at a 360×800 device viewport Chrome scales the 1,241px layout to 0.29, making text and controls tiny.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, initial-scale=1, remove fixed 1,240px page assumptions, and rebuild key grids with intrinsic fluid sizing.

findings.summary: Components rely on physical fixed-layout CSS rather than container-responsive composition.
findings.evidence: CSS probes on all five templates found no @container/container-type signal and hundreds of physical left/right declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type on reusable card/list regions and @container rules for compact and expanded variants.

findings.summary: Touch targets and keyboard focus are not reliably usable.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe counted 331 visible controls below 24px in at least one dimension and all first 25 sampled controls had no visible outline or box shadow after focus; breaking news had 517 small targets.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide visible :focus-visible styles and increase interactive hit areas to at least 24×24 CSS px, preferably 44×44 for primary mobile controls.

findings.summary: Reading primary content is gated by a full-page consent decision.
findings.evidence: Every representative editorial path loaded behind the same blocking consent interstitial; the article’s rendered screenshot is not readable until a choice is made.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep core news content readable while consent choices are pending and defer non-essential advertising/personalization requests until a choice.

findings.summary: Load and interaction performance are far outside good ranges.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured homepage performance 0.23, LCP 11.3s, TBT 2,040ms, Speed Index 25.4s and TTI 60.1s; the article scored 0.10 with LCP 9.6s, TBT 2,740ms and CLS 0.32.
findings.suggestedFix: Set performance budgets, prioritize the LCP asset, eliminate non-essential startup scripts, and delay ad/recommendation stacks until after core content is interactive.

findings.summary: Article content shifts substantially during load.
findings.evidence: The mobile article layout observer recorded CLS 0.466, including a single 0.286 shift; all 23 sampled article images lacked width/height attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image/ad/media space with width, height, and aspect-ratio; use metric-compatible font fallbacks and avoid late insertion above content.

findings.summary: Heavy scripting repeatedly blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded 23 long tasks, a 161ms longest task, and 662ms trace TBT; Lighthouse measured 2,040–2,740ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile script execution, remove or delay low-value third parties, split long tasks, and schedule remaining work by user-visible priority.

findings.summary: The homepage transfers an excessive network and image payload.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 607 requests and 16.98MB transferred: 403 image requests/10.27MB and 80 scripts/5.46MB. The image audit found 99/100 without dimensions, 79 below-fold images not lazy, 30 oversized, and 76 without srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold media, emit responsive srcset/sizes and explicit dimensions, consolidate requests, cache immutable assets, and prioritize only the LCP image.

findings.summary: Large amounts of unused JavaScript and CSS ship on initial load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 2,809KiB unused JavaScript and 500KiB unused CSS on home, and 2,935KiB unused JavaScript/568KiB CSS on the article.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split template code, remove duplicate/legacy bundles, and conditionally load ad, video, accessibility, and recommendation integrations only where needed.

findings.summary: Important links, buttons, and images lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse home found 20 unnamed links, 3 unnamed buttons, and 9 images without alt; article image inspection reported 11/23 without alt (including third-party player assets).
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate accessible names and meaningful alt, hide decorative/duplicate assets from assistive technology, and verify third-party embeds expose usable controls.

findings.summary: Text contrast fails on representative surfaces.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found five insufficient-contrast nodes on home and two on article; accessibility scores were 0.61 and 0.80.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust semantic foreground/background tokens to meet WCAG AA in all states and verify them in light, dark, and high-contrast modes.

findings.summary: Mobile reflow and media accessibility are seriously compromised.
findings.evidence: width=1240 forces browser shrink-to-fit on 360px screens; probes found hundreds of undersized targets and two article videos without caption tracks.
findings.suggestedFix: Enable device-width reflow and user scaling, enlarge targets, and supply captions/transcripts for editorial video.

findings.summary: Representative pages log many browser errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 16 console errors on home and 7 on article; source-map processing also reported out-of-bounds mappings.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix runtime/network errors, publish correct source maps, and add console-error regression checks for each template.

findings.summary: Document assets are not soundly sized and browser inspector issues remain.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 99/100 homepage images without width/height and 30 oversized; Lighthouse reported inspector issues and broken source-map mappings.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic dimensions and correctly sized responsive assets, repair source maps, and resolve DevTools inspector/deprecation findings.

findings.summary: Mobile and crawler signals are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found six non-crawlable links on home and two on article; the site declares width=1240 rather than device-width, and raw-content coverage was only 4–10%.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href links, device-width viewport metadata, and server-render the primary article/listing content rather than only metadata and a thin shell.

findings.summary: The standard sitemap endpoint is missing and robots.txt does not advertise an alternative.
findings.evidence: GET /sitemap.xml returned the HTML 404 page; robots.txt returned 200 but contained no Sitemap directive.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a current XML sitemap (or sitemap index) and advertise its absolute URL in robots.txt.

findings.summary: The login template has no meta description.
findings.evidence: The login probe found a descriptive title but an empty/missing meta description; editorial templates had both.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise, unique meta description for the sign-in/subscription entry template.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie attributes are materially incomplete.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and frame restrictions are present, but HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent; 13/13 observed cookies were flagged insecure and several are long-lived SameSite=None analytics cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS and nosniff, explicit Referrer/Permissions policies, strengthen CSP beyond frame-ancestors, and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure with the narrowest workable SameSite.

findings.summary: The page activates an extreme tracking and third-party footprint before a clear rejection choice.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 71 third-party origins and 27 known tracker endpoints; HAR recorded 607 requests. Initial consent UI has no reject action, while Manage options exposes 289 toggles with 63 checked.
findings.suggestedFix: Default non-essential purposes off, add an equally prominent Reject all action, block tracker requests until valid consent, and remove vendors without measurable editorial value.

findings.summary: The account flow offers email/social sign-in but no passkey path.
findings.evidence: The visible login surface offers email, Google, and Apple; source and UI probes found no passkey text or navigator.credentials/PublicKeyCredential integration.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey registration and conditional authentication while retaining account-recovery and federated fallbacks.

findings.summary: Core article and listing content is largely unavailable without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured raw-content overlap of 4% for article and 5% for news, classified both as JS shells; crawler screenshots are blank while rendered screenshots contain the page/modal.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the complete headline, article body, byline, key media alternatives, and listing links; layer interactivity and ads on afterward.

findings.summary: Hebrew pages compute left-to-right direction and depend heavily on physical CSS.
findings.evidence: All five probes report lang=he but computed dir=ltr; article CSS signal found 1,032 physical left/right declarations versus 4 logical-property uses.
findings.suggestedFix: Set dir=rtl on the root and migrate layout to inline/block logical properties, testing mixed Hebrew/Latin content and controls.

findings.summary: Consent choices are asymmetric and many purposes are preselected.
findings.evidence: Initial UI offers Consent and Manage options, not Reject all. Manage options shows Accept all/Confirm choices and 289 toggles, 63 checked.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide equally prominent Accept all and Reject all controls, default optional purposes off, group vendors intelligibly, and keep refusal as easy as acceptance.

findings.summary: Submitting the empty email step provides no visible or accessible error state.
findings.evidence: After activating Continue with an empty visible email field, the field still reported valid=true, no aria-invalid/describedby, no alert, and focus did not move to the field.
findings.suggestedFix: Use required/type=email validation after interaction, move focus to the invalid field, set aria-invalid/aria-describedby, and announce a specific correction in a live region.

findings.summary: The visible email sign-in field omits autocomplete metadata.
findings.evidence: Login probe found type=email with an empty autocomplete attribute; no passkey-assisted flow was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=email or username as appropriate and add webauthn to the token when conditional passkey UI is supported.

findings.summary: Image delivery is wasteful for a text-led news homepage.
findings.evidence: 403 image requests transferred 10.27MB; 99/100 audited images were classified legacy, 30 oversized, 76 missing srcset, and 79 below-fold images not lazy.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt responsive format=auto/AVIF/WebP delivery, right-size each slot, lazy-load below the fold, and remove duplicate hidden image instances.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts and background work dominate the resource budget.
findings.evidence: 71 third-party origins, 80 scripts/5.46MB and 607 total requests were observed; ten repeated scroll cycles added 74 resource entries and raised live DOM nodes from 13,735 to 16,209.
findings.suggestedFix: Create a vendor budget, remove low-value integrations, load ads/recommendations only near view, and stop background work when hidden or consent is absent.

findings.summary: Repeated navigation-like scrolling grows retained heap and DOM materially.
findings.evidence: Garbage-collected heap summaries grew from 147.4MB/2.05M nodes to 163.8MB/2.33M after ten top-to-bottom cycles; in-session used heap rose 124.5MB→179.3MB and DOM nodes 13,735→16,209.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile retained paths after repeated feed traversal, dispose players/ads/listeners on exit, bound caches, and virtualize or remove offscreen feed modules.

findings.summary: The initial page footprint is disproportionate for a news index.
findings.evidence: Baseline heap after garbage collection contained 2,051,937 nodes and 147.4MB self size; live DOM contained 13,735 elements before scrolling.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce duplicate hidden DOM, virtualize long lists, defer recommendation/ad trees, and avoid instantiating media players until requested or near view.

taskList.title: Rebuild mobile layout around device-width reflow and accessible targets
Cut startup network, script, image, tracker and memory cost
Make consent symmetric, non-blocking and privacy-preserving
Server-render complete article and listing content
Repair accessibility names, contrast, focus and captions
Harden security headers and cookie policy
Repair crawl/index metadata and sitemap delivery
